question: emergency-lighting-exit-signage
unit: ea (per emergency fitting, averaged across 28 downlights + 12 exit signs)

band.unit: ea (per emergency fitting, averaged across 28 downlights + 12 exit signs)
band.basis: Auckland, GST exclusive, 40 fittings (28 maintained LED emergency downlights + 12 maintained LED exit signs), 800 m2 single-storey commercial fitout. Sum of the eleven priced components = $12,721 low / $19,354 high for the 40-fitting scope; divided by 40 = $318-$484 per fitting ($12,720-$19,350 total). All main cost drivers are cited: fittings from QV LED Emergency Lighting t20 (28 x $208-$236 downlights; 12 x $208-$347 exit signs), cable from QV Cable: Copper t7 (480 m at $6.60-$9.40/m), breakers from QV Control Equipment t29, access plant from QV Preliminaries t8, electrician time from QV Labour Rates at $83.65/hr, and the discharge test plus CoC/ESC from fetched pages. Allowances total only $280-$680 (about 2-3.5% of the band), well under a third. The top end deliberately stacks every adverse assumption (larger 5 W exit sign, a wired test switch at all 40 fittings, the dearer cable row, 3 days of lift hire, the $25/fitting test rate) - a realistic outturn on a clear void and a single continuous visit sits nearer $370-$430 per fitting. Confidence medium, not high, because: QV electrical rows are unreviewed composites whose inclusions (install labour, battery duration, viewing distance) are unstated; the test rate is from the Australian market; and if the consent requires fire-rated emergency sub-circuit wiring instead of the specified 1.5 mm2 TPS, the cable line moves from about $3.2k to about $26k and this band is void. Suppliers to ring to firm the fitting and test-switch lines: Clevertronics NZ, Legrand New Zealand, Schneider Electric NZ, and wholesalers Ideal Electrical / JA Russell / Radcliffe Electrical; for the certification line, the installing licensed electrical contractor or an independent IQP.

band.unit: ea (per emergency fitting, averaged over 28 downlights + 12 exit signs)
band.basis: Sum of nine separately priced components on a per-fitting basis: 0.7 emergency downlight + 0.3 exit sign supplied and installed (QV installed rates), 12 m of installed 1.5 mm2 TPS emergency sub-circuit, one manual test switch per fitting, 3 x 16 A MCB amortised, scissor-platform access amortised, the initial 90-minute discharge test and AS/NZS 2293.2 documentation built from the QV electrician hourly rate, the CoC/ESC certificate fee, and a small sundries allowance. 40 fittings = $13,500 to $21,600, midpoint about $438/ea ($17,500). All figures GST exclusive, Auckland. Only one component is an allowance (sundries, 1.5-3% of the band), so the band is driven by QV rows; the widest single swing is cable, where the two QV 1.5 mm2 TPS installed rows ($6.60/m two-core+earth vs $14.20/m three-core+earth) differ by 115%. Confidence is medium, not high: the QV rows are unreviewed, the exit-sign rows do not state viewing distance, the QV cable row descriptors do not say whether terminations are included, and the resulting band sits above the brief's pinned $315-430 because the brief's $48/ea cable line is a material-only figure against QV's installed $79-$170 for 12 m. Excludes GST, preliminaries, margin, design, consent, BWOF/IQP, the initial inspection and Compliance Schedule entry, ongoing re-testing, central battery/inverter/addressable or self-test monitoring, new DB or sub-main, ceiling grid alteration and decoration, and fire alarm interface.

band.unit: ea (blended per emergency fitting: 28 downlights + 12 exit signs, 40 fittings, Auckland, NZD GST excl.)
band.basis: Low $13,539 / High $17,281 for the 40-fitting scope ($338-$432 per fitting; midpoint $385/ea, $15,410 total). Built from QV installed rates: 28 x $236 emergency downlight (t20:r7), 12 x $208-$347 exit sign (t20:r11 / t20:r12), 480m x $6.60-$8.25/m 1.5mm2 2C+E TPS installed in the ceiling void (t7:r71), 3 x $53 MCB (t29:r33), 2-5 days x $94/day electric scissor lift (t8:r2), plus two allowances (DB terminations $120-$320; initial discharge test/log book/CoC+ESC $800-$1,400) which are under a third of the total. All QV rows are unreviewed and the luminaire rows are read as supply-and-install. Low assumes a clear void, short pulls and one continuous install visit; high assumes a congested void, occupied-tenancy/split access and out-of-hours working, and the upper exit-sign row. Excludes GST, preliminaries, margin, design, consent, BWOF/IQP fees, ongoing re-testing, central battery/inverter/addressable systems, new board or sub-main, ceiling grid alteration or redecoration, and fire alarm interface.
